## Why this matters

Participants trust us with their time, their bodies and their personal data. A single careless email or shared spreadsheet can break that trust, harm a participant, and put the whole lab's research permission at risk. These rules follow EU and Hungarian law (including the GDPR), and they apply to everyone, including students.

## Research ethics approval [BA]{.ba-tag}

- All research that involves data collection must be approved by the [Research Ethics Committee](https://www.ppk.elte.hu/en/research-ethics-committee) of the Faculty. This includes student projects.
- Only the head of the lab can submit an ethics application.
- Data collection can only happen with supervision, and only after the permission is granted.

## Accounts and permissions [BA]{.ba-tag}

- **Never log in** to your own or the lab's account on someone else's computer. It can compromise passwords and makes the event history hard to keep tidy.
- Use accounts with your own identity, for example your own Google account.
- Documents are shared on Google Drive or OSF with each project participant individually. That way, we have an accurate log of who did what.
- Permissions are removed when you leave a project.
- If you really have no choice but to log in on a computer that isn't yours, use an incognito window (Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome) and log out afterwards.

## File sharing and ownership [BA]{.ba-tag}

- Project files are kept in Google Drive and OSF.
- **As soon as data collection starts**, the ownership of key project files and folders must be transferred to the lab account ({{< var links.lab_email >}}).
- The reason: these files are often needed years later, and the lab must keep access even after students leave the lab or the university.
- Key project participants keep access as long as needed. Those who leave the project lose access.

## Data security and privacy [BA]{.ba-tag}

- Never give confidential information, such as participant information or passwords, to third parties or unauthorized people.
- When working with confidential information, use a password on your computer and, preferably, two-factor authentication on cloud services.
- Keep your passwords secret.
- Recorded data should be anonymized as soon as possible. After that, it can be made public.
- **Non-anonymized data and private participant information must never be shared with anyone, not even within the lab.**
- Personal identifiers (email, Neptun code, etc.) must never be used as the ID variable in a dataset. Module 6 shows how to create proper IDs.

## Do

These tasks are also in your ClickUp onboarding task.

- [ ] Turn on two-factor authentication for your Google account.
- [ ] Make sure your laptop has a login password and locks automatically.
- [ ] Read the Faculty's [Research Ethics Committee page](https://www.ppk.elte.hu/en/research-ethics-committee).

## Check yourself

::: quiz
A participant emails you their name and Neptun code to ask about their course credit. A fellow RA asks you to forward the email so they can handle it. What do you do?

- [ ] Forward it; they're a lab member.
- [ ] Post it in the project Slack channel so the whole team knows.
- [x] Don't forward personal data; handle it yourself or ask the project supervisor how participant contacts are managed.

::: explain
Private participant information must not be shared with anyone, not even within the lab. Only the people responsible for that data should handle it.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Data collection for your study starts next week. What has to happen with the project's Google Drive folder?

- [ ] Nothing, as long as you remain the owner.
- [x] Ownership of the key files and folders is transferred to the lab's account.
- [ ] It should be downloaded and stored on a USB drive as a backup.

::: explain
From the start of data collection, the lab account must own key project files, so the lab never loses access when people leave.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Which of these are acceptable? Select every acceptable option.

- [x] Sharing a project document with a co-author via their own Google account.
- [ ] Logging into the lab's Google account on a friend's laptop to grab a file.
- [x] Publishing a dataset on OSF after it has been fully anonymized.
- [ ] Using participants' email addresses as the ID column so it's easy to match records.

::: explain
Share with individuals' own accounts and publish only anonymized data. Never log in to accounts on other people's computers, and never use personal identifiers as IDs.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Your BA thesis project is "just a small questionnaire study". Does it need ethics approval?

- [ ] No, student projects are exempt.
- [ ] Only if it collects health data.
- [x] Yes. All research involving data collection needs approval from the Faculty's Research Ethics Committee.

::: explain
The rule explicitly includes student projects. No approval, no data collection.
:::
:::
